History:
- Chief complaint: Acute worsening lower abdominal pain for several days.
- Onset/duration: Pain began a few days ago; progressively worsening; constant.
- Location: Central lower abdomen (below the umbilicus).
- Severity: Pain rated up to 8/10.
- Associated symptoms: Nausea (no vomiting); light vaginal bleeding/discharge; previous constipation last week but currently resolving; regular activity otherwise.
- Menstrual/gynecologic history: Last period approximately 2–3 weeks ago (reports vary); on Implant (Implanon) for about 1 year; periods described as irregular but present since implant; light pink vaginal bleeding noted; one prior pregnancy test about 1 month ago.
- Contraception: Implanon in place; no medication changes mentioned.
- Obstetric history: No pregnancies.
- Allergies: Amoxicillin allergy.
- Medications: No other medications documented.
- Social/history factors: Occupation—teacher; lives with husband and his family; recently abroad (over a year ago); intake of alcohol/tobacco not clearly documented.
- Red flags/other: Denies fever, cough, shortness of breath, chest pain, or fainting; no difficulty breathing reported.

Past Medical History:
- Allergies: Amoxicillin.
- Chronic illnesses: None documented.
- Prior surgeries/hospitalizations: None documented.
- Current medications: Implanon contraception; no other meds documented.

Physical Examination:
- Not yet performed; plan for in-person abdominal examination.
- Documented negatives: No reported fever; no shortness of breath; no fainting on standing; patient able to attend consultation in a private setting.
- Note: No objective examination findings provided in the transcript.

Impression:
- Acute lower abdominal pain of unclear etiology in a reproductive-age female on Implanon, with light vaginal bleeding and nausea; evaluation with abdominal examination and pregnancy testing planned.

Management Plan:
- Arrange a face-to-face abdominal examination in clinic to assess cause of pain.
- Obtain a pregnancy test today; if positive, patient should be seen urgently.
- Schedule appointment via support line.
- Advise management if symptoms worsen (inability to keep fluids down) or if pain progresses before the appointment.
- No medications prescribed at this visit; continue usual contraception.

Patient Summary:
- A 23-year-old woman on Implanon presents with several days of progressively worsening lower abdominal pain (8/10) with nausea and light vaginal bleeding. She previously had a pregnancy test about a month ago. A face-to-face abdominal exam and a pregnancy test today are planned; urgent evaluation if pregnancy test is positive or if symptoms worsen.

Key Takeaways:
- Arrange and complete an in-person abdominal exam and a today pregnancy test.
- If pregnancy test is positive, seek urgent evaluation.
- Seek urgent care if pain worsens or if she cannot keep fluids down before the scheduled appointment.

Next Steps:
- Conduct in-clinic abdominal examination.
- Perform pregnancy test today; act on results (urgent if positive).
- Schedule and complete the outpatient appointment; follow-up based on exam findings and test results.
